blocks.text: 1. Recall At K

blocks.alt: All relevant chunks compare against retrieved relevant chunks to produce a recall score
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785439734392-879020461.png

Precision At K closed by drawing the exact line between what precision measures and what it does not. Recall at K, the fraction of all actually relevant chunks that were retrieved within the top K, is that other measure, completing the pair.
It counts how many of every relevant chunk in the whole knowledge base actually appear in the retrieved set.
2. Recall Needs The Entire Set Of Relevant Chunks
Precision at K only needs to know which retrieved chunks are relevant.
Recall at K additionally needs to know every relevant chunk that exists in the whole knowledge base.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Metric","What it needs to know"],"rows":[["Precision at K","Which retrieved chunks are relevant"],["Recall at K","Every relevant chunk that exists, retrieved or not"]]}

blocks.text: 3. The Denominator Differs From Precision

blocks.alt: Precision divides by retrieved count while recall divides by total relevant count
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785439734392-876191533.png
Precision at K divides by K, the number retrieved, while recall at K divides by the total number of relevant chunks that actually exist.
Two metrics answering two different questions with two different denominators.
4. A High Recall Can Still Mean A Low Precision

blocks.alt: High recall is compared against low precision
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785439734392-774486634.png
Retrieving every relevant chunk along with many irrelevant ones scores perfect recall.
A perfect recall score can still coexist with a low precision score at the same K.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.content: Retrieving fifty chunks that happen to include every relevant one, scores perfect recall, even though forty five of those fifty chunks being irrelevant means a very low precision at the same time.
blocks.text: Retrieving fifty chunks that happen to include every relevant one scores perfect recall, even though forty five of those fifty chunks being irrelevant means a very low precision at the same time.
5. Increasing K Almost Always Raises Recall

blocks.alt: A small K is compared against a large K, which gives higher recall
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785439734393-923028682.png
Retrieving more chunks can only add relevant chunks to the set, never remove them.
Recall at K is monotonically non-decreasing as K grows larger.
6. Recall Matters Most For Multi-Hop Questions

blocks.alt: A single-fact question is compared against a multi-hop question needing high recall
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785439734654-787010299.png
As with multi-hop questions benefit most in Chain Of Thought, a question needing every one of several facts fails completely if even one relevant chunk is missed.
Recall at K directly measures whether that complete coverage was achieved.

blocks.text: 7. Precision Recall Tradeoff In Practice

blocks.alt: Precision is traded off against recall
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785439734655-789792530.png
As with reducing the chance of an irrelevant chunk influencing the answer in Advanced RAG, raising K to improve recall also lowers precision by adding more irrelevant chunks.
The two metrics pull against each other as K changes.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.content: Raising K from five to twenty, tends to raise recall by catching more relevant chunks while lowering precision as more irrelevant chunks get pulled in alongside them.
blocks.text: Raising K from five to twenty tends to raise recall by catching more relevant chunks while lowering precision as more irrelevant chunks get pulled in alongside them.
8. Averaging Recall Across Many Queries
As with averaging precision across many queries in Precision At K, a single query's recall score says little about the system as a whole.
Averaging recall at K across a real evaluation set gives a trustworthy system level number.
9. Recognizing When Recall At K Is The Right Metric To Track

blocks.alt: Not being able to miss relevant info points toward tracking recall at K
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785439734656-449888043.png
Tasks where missing a relevant fact is costly benefit from tracking recall.
Tasks where irrelevant noise matters more should track precision instead.

blocks.text: 11. Common Mistakes

items: Reporting recall at K without knowing the true, complete set of relevant chunks.
Assuming a perfect recall score also implies good precision at the same K.
Raising K to chase better recall without checking the resulting hit to precision.
Judging system quality from a single query's recall score instead of averaging over many.

blocks.text: 12. Key Takeaways

items: Recall at K is the fraction of all actually relevant chunks that were retrieved within the top K.
Recall needs the entire set of relevant chunks, not just which retrieved ones are relevant.
Precision divides by K; recall divides by the total number of relevant chunks that exist.
A perfect recall score can still coexist with low precision if many irrelevant chunks were also retrieved.
Recall at K is monotonically non-decreasing as K grows larger.
Recall matters most for questions needing every one of several facts to be found.
Raising K to improve recall typically lowers precision, the two metrics pulling against each other.
Averaging recall at K across a real evaluation set gives a trustworthy system level number.
